findings.title: [P1] Subtract allowed lateness from the tenant watermark
findings.comment: The contract in /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/windows.py:25-29 permits timestamps at or above watermark minus allowed_lateness, but line 70 adds it. With lateness 30, independently tested timestamps [100, 70, 90, 110] produce acceptance [true, false, false, false] instead of all true. dropped_late becomes 3 and the early return leaves the tenant watermark at 100 instead of 110. The base implementation used subtraction, so this is an introduced data-loss regression.

findings.title: [P1] Clear pending windows after taking the flush snapshot
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/aggregate.py:85-87 removed the previous pending-state clear, contradicting its retirement contract and the batch semantics in /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/pipeline.py:20-23. Independently tested separate batches at timestamps 1 and 61 plus an empty batch: output starts were [[0], [0, 60], [0, 60]], not [[0], [60], []]. Separate batches in the same window with values 2 and 3 produced second-batch count 2 and total 5 instead of count 1 and total 3. Each new-window batch also retains historical state and copies it again, yielding quadratic cumulative output growth.

findings.title: [P2] Load tenant configuration outside the per-reading loop
findings.comment: /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/pipeline.py:39-40 calls load_tenant_limits for every reading before clipping or lateness checks. /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/tenants.py:36-37 opens and parses the entire configuration without caching. Independent instrumentation confirmed 1,000 configuration opens and parses for 1,000 readings from one tenant. Thus static configuration incurs synchronous I/O per record and parsing work proportional to reading count times configuration size. No per-reading refresh requirement is documented; this is an introduced ingestion-efficiency defect.

Examine the per-reading configuration-loading path in /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/pipeline.py and /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/tenants.py for ingest costs that scale with stream size.
